name: cointegration_residual_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs (stocks that share a long-run equilibrium despite short-term divergences) provide mean-reversion opportunities when their spread deviates from equilibrium. Unlike correlation, cointegration implies a stable long-run relationship. By applying the Johansen cointegration test to 20-day rolling 1-min data for pre-screened NIFTY 50 pairs (same sector, similar market cap), and trading the spread when the normalized residual exceeds ± 2 sigma, we capture spread reversion. The inefficiency exists because cointegration testing requires econometric expertise, and maintaining a real-time cointegration-adjusted spread across multiple pairs is infrastructure-heavy.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs within same GICS sector (e.g., HDFCBANK-ICICIBANK, TCS-INFOSYS)
stock_filter: Both pair members: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; Johansen test p-value < 0.05 on 20-day rolling data

indicators.name: Coint_Vector
indicators.params: Johansen cointegration vector (beta) from trace test, estimated on 20-day rolling 1-min data

indicators.name: Coint_PValue
indicators.params: Johansen trace test p-value (re-estimated daily before session)

conditions: Spread_Zscore < -2.0 (spread significantly below equilibrium — long A, short B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further down: Spread_Zscore > min(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
long.confirmation: Spread_Zscore turns up: Spread_Zscore > Spread_Zscore[2 bars ago]

conditions: Spread_Zscore > 2.0 (spread significantly above equilibrium — short A, long B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further up: Spread_Zscore < max(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
short.confirmation: Spread_Zscore turns down: Spread_Zscore < Spread_Zscore[2 bars ago]

entry.entry_price: simultaneous market orders on both legs (long A + short B, or vice versa)

exit.target: Spread_Zscore reverts to 0 (spread returns to equilibrium)
exit.stop_loss: Spread_Zscore reaches -3.5 for long spread / +3.5 for short spread

risk.position_sizing: Equal notional on both legs: ₹50K long + ₹50K short; scale with abs(Spread_Zscore): larger deviation = larger size, capped at ₹75K per leg

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, cointegration relationships may temporarily break
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 60 bars for spread statistics) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Both stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20) on entry bar
filters.trend_filter: None — pairs trade is market-neutral by construction
filters.event_filter: Skip pair if either stock has earnings today or tomorrow
other_filters: Coint_Vector must be re-estimated daily; intraday drift in beta is possible but assumed small

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — pairs trading is well-known; the edge is in the cointegration-based spread construction (vs simple ratio/price difference) and the intraday application with proper Johansen testing

weaknesses: Cointegration is a long-run property (typically tested on daily data over months/years) — testing on 20 days of 1-min data may detect spurious cointegration that is not economically meaningful
Two-legged execution doubles transaction costs (slippage and brokerage on both legs) and creates execution risk — if one leg fills and the other doesn't, you have unhedged directional exposure
Cointegration vectors (beta) estimated on historical data may drift within the session — if beta changes from 0.9 to 1.0, the spread signal is miscalibrated and entries may be premature
prior_art: Johansen (1991) cointegration test; Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading; Vidyamurthy (2004) 'Pairs Trading'; intraday cointegration applications in Avellaneda & Lee (2010)
notes: The biggest practical challenge is simultaneous execution of both legs — consider using a smart order router that submits both legs atomically. Pre-screen pairs daily and maintain a watchlist of 5-10 cointegrated pairs to monitor during the session.
